previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text: (codex-17's flat progress) You're reading it correctly: since my pin, no row has gone from failing to compiling. Part of the reason is my design. The "fixed, awaiting re-probe" band in `progress.py` treats a merged fix as clearing all 43 rows that share an error message. In fact each fix only moves those rows to their next failure. The 20/44/19/27 line therefore showed fixes landing, not constants compiling. codex-17 has diagnosed this correctly, and its change of approach is the right one.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text:
(the new approach from line 556) I agree with three of its changes:
- **Stopping the full re-probe.** Five probes took 14 minutes and none compiled.
- **Following one sample row through each successive failure** until it compiles.
- **Reporting what changed in each row** (failure X → failure Y) instead of the band totals.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text:
(two things I'd flag to it) Both come from the probe table, which I read this turn:
1. **builtin7 may have leaked an internal port name.** `testParseModuleAux.parse` at `065ed16` fails with "unsupported parsed Lean match pattern 'DeferredCompilerBuiltinCandidate'". That is the Python class builtin7 introduced, and it is turning up where a Lean pattern should be. That row should be re-probed at `5c94457` before more work builds on builtin7.
2. **Two failures now account for every sampled row.** "stuck `Decidable (Eq ?m ?m)`" appears on `mkDeclExt`, `mkSimprocExt` and `PersistentHashMap.foldl`. The "source projection" error appears on `CacheExtension.register`, `mkDeclSetExt` and `addParserTokens`. Fixing those two is the shortest route to the count moving. The `Decidable` case is a fix that didn't hold: `69af4db` was supposed to cover it, so a discovery job on why it still fails comes before any new fix.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text: (wasted jobs) linki4 spent a whole job on a defect that `cc05e83` had already fixed. Its brief was based on a probe from an older commit. A cheap rule would prevent that: every discovery brief re-probes its target row at the current HEAD before investigating.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text: (one decision) Shall I bell codex-17 these two flags plus the re-probe rule? It's one short bell with no new dispatch. Or you can paste this paragraph into its buffer yourself.
